40:1.3.1.text: Dan Marolt. Company. Nice. Gave me his card.
40:1.3.1.when: Fact: Dan is with the company

40:1.3.2.text: Wade. Security for the company. Says he doesn't go on the water.
40:1.3.2.when: Fact: Wade does the company's security

40:1.3.3.text: W. Helstrom was at the bunkhouse the week Walt went. And at the funeral.
40:1.3.3.when: Fact: Wade is W. Helstrom of 2019

40:1.3.5.text: The ring is Carl Brekke. He ran the old outfit's office.
40:1.3.5.when: Fact: The old man with the ring is Brekke, and he ran Boreal

40:1.3.6.text: Thursday is Len. He tells the ring what I ask.

40:1.3.7.text: Tasha saw it in the numbers last year. They told her to drop it.
40:1.3.7.when: Fact: Tasha flagged the old stations

40:1.3.8.text: Frank works nights for the company. Says he's retired.
40:1.3.8.when: Fact: Frank works nights for the company

40:3.1.1.text: You must be the one with the old outfitter gear. Small town. I'm Dan. I'm with the company.

40:3.1.2.text: Northmark. The new sign at the junction. It's been up ten years and everybody still calls it the new sign.
40:3.1.2.if: gives: the fact "Dan Marolt, Northmark, community relations"

40:3.1.c2.text: How do you know who I am?

40:3.1.3.text: You've got a pack older than me with a crew stencil on it. People notice old gear up here. I noticed.

40:3.1.4.text: Also my sister-in-law does the books at two of these places. I'm kidding. Mostly.

40:3.1.5.text: Nothing. Coffee. To say hi. We sponsor the peewee team, we do the food shelf in November. I like to know who's around.

40:3.1.c4.text: Did you know a guide named Walt?

40:3.1.6.text: Walt? Sure, I knew of him. Sad thing. Those big lakes in October.

40:3.1.7.text: My dad knew him a little. Said he was the only guide in Ely who'd take a client back to the same lake two days running if the fish were there.

40:3.1.8.text: The old outfit. Before my time. Way before. There's a lot of old stories about the company back then. Most of them are about men who're dead now.

40:3.1.9.text: My grandpa was underground at the Pioneer thirty years. My kids want to stay up here. So, yeah. Done right, I'm for it.

40:3.1.10.text: Ask me if I'd want it done wrong. I wouldn't. That's not a speech, that's my kids.

40:3.1.12.text: Listen, if you come across any old junk from the drill days, core, a casing, one of those old crew stencils, bring it by. We're putting a little history wall up at the office. I'll pay you for it. Fair.

40:3.1.13.text: Can I buy you a coffee? No? Another time. I'm around.

40:3.1.14.text: That's Dan. He's all right. He coached my nephew. Don't sell him anything you'd miss.

40:3.2.1.text: That's one of theirs. Look at the threads on that. They don't make pipe like that any more.

40:3.2.2.text: Gabbro. My grandpa'd know what it is to the inch. I know it's a rock.

40:3.2.3.text: Boreal Range Minerals. Huh. I've only ever seen that on a letterhead in a box.
40:3.2.3.when: Item: Photo of the BRM-14 patch

40:3.2.4.text: This is going right on the wall. With your name, if you want. No? Fair enough.

40:3.2.5.if: This tells the player the company wants them. Walt page, once: "Dan would buy Walt's journals. He said 'if there were any'."

40:3.4.c2.text: One man, boots. Sat a long while.

notice.openhouse.text:
NORTHMARK METALS
COMMUNITY OPEN HOUSE
Saturday 22 August · 10 to 2 · Farm Lake, the big room
Coffee and bars · Kids welcome · Meet our geologists · See the Kettle project
Ask us anything.

40:3.5.1.text: You came! Coffee's there, bars are there, the good bars are gone, that's on the Lutheran ladies.

40:3.5.2.text: Ask me somewhere that isn't here.

40:3.5.3.text: Here, I'll ring the old pads for you. That's all public.

40:3.5.5.text: My daughter teaches third grade. Fourteen kids. Used to be thirty. If this fills the room, I'll eat their bars all day.

40:3.5.6.text: I came for the coffee and to look at them. I've looked.

40:3.5.7.text: Fifty years they've been telling us next year. I'll believe it when there's a lunch bucket in it.

40:3.5.8.text: Water goes downhill. They can put that on a poster too.

40:3.5.c1.text: Old man with a gold ring.

40:3.5.9.text: You'll be the one with the old gear. Len says you've been asking about Bald Eagle. Lovely lake. Cold.

40:3.5.10.text: Walt was the best line-cutter I ever had. Shame about his brother. Those big lakes in October.

40:3.5.11.text: Quiet man. He'd cut a straight line through a cedar swamp and never say a word about the bugs.

40:3.5.12.text: The younger Haapala. A hothead. Good kid. Hothead.

40:3.5.13.text: Everybody up here was young once and did what the office said. Not him. That's not a compliment, at my age. It was then.

40:3.5.c4.text: What did you do at Boreal?

40:3.5.14.text: Ran the office. Signed the timesheets. Ate a lot of soup.

40:3.5.15.text: Mining school, 1961. They gave us these to remind us what we were for.

40:3.5.c6.text: What do you do for Northmark?

40:3.5.16.text: I tell young people where the old holes are so they don't drill them twice.

40:3.5.17.text: If you ever find what that family thought they had, you'll find it's old paper. Old paper burns.

40:3.5.19.text: Walt thought a lot of things mattered. He was a guide. They're sentimental.
40:3.5.19.if: gives: Len's next Thursday report says the player is careful. No change in the world. The rumour line "careful" is Brekke's word and can come back once through Len: "Carl says you're careful. He meant it nice."

40:3.6.1.text: If you're here for the gate, there's no gate. People keep asking.

40:3.6.2.text: Field geologist. Northmark. I'm from Tower. My dad drove haul truck on the Range twenty-six years. I'm the first geologist in the family.

40:3.6.3.text: I'm for the mine if it's done right. Checking it's done right is the job. I'm good at the job.

40:3.6.4.text: Water. Same creek every month. You can't say what you changed if you don't know what it was.

40:3.6.5.text: Background means before anybody touched it. Clean or dirty, it's the creek on its own.

40:3.6.6.text: If you call a dirty creek background, you get to put dirtier water in it later. That's all. That's the whole trick, if somebody wanted one.
40:3.6.6.if: gives: the plain meaning of the stakes. Walt page: "'Background' means before anyone touched it. If a dirty station is called background, the rules get looser."

40:3.6.c4.text: Who's the man in the clean boots?

40:3.6.7.text: Wade? He's a contractor. Security. He doesn't come to the safety meetings and nobody's ever seen him on a boat.

40:3.6.8.text: I don't know what he does. I know I don't want to.

40:3.6.10.text: Last year I put the old stations next to the upstream ones. The ones they call background are dirtier. Not a little.

40:3.6.11.text: I wrote it up. I got a meeting and a nice lunch and told it was 'already characterised'. Drop it.

40:3.6.12.text: I dropped it. I have a mortgage. Don't put my name on anything.
40:3.6.12.if: gives: the fact for the Walt page, 1.3; flag `tashaTold`. If the player tells Maggie, see 6.6. In the journalist ending she leads the new sampling, as the bible says.

40:3.7.1.text: Hey. You look like you've been out a while. Good out there?

40:3.7.2.text: Can I ask you a work thing? Thirty seconds.

40:3.7.3.text: If you ever came across anything from the old exploration days, papers, field books, maps, somebody's box of whatever, we'd want it back. For the history. We'd pay. More than fair.

40:3.7.4.text: A thousand dollars. For anything real. Legal gets nervous about old stuff floating around. It's company property, technically. Proprietary exploration data.

40:3.7.5.text: Honestly? I don't know. Nobody's told me. I say a thousand bucks for a box of old paper is a good day for somebody.

40:3.7.7.text: The office. The Cities. Somebody with a nicer chair than mine.

40:3.7.c7.text: Why do you care so much?

40:3.7.8.text: I don't, personally. I care that it's my job, and my job's the reason there's a hockey team.

40:3.7.9.text: Offer's good till the snow. After that I can't promise anything. Not up to me.

40:3.7.10.text: You look tired. You all right? You look like you slept in a canoe.

40:3.7.11.text: Listen. That thing I said, about the old stuff? If it's ever more than junk, you call me before you call anybody. I can't tell you a number. I can tell you they'd find one.

40:3.7.12.text: I don't know what any of it is. I'm saying it because I'd rather it was you got paid than nobody.
40:3.7.12.if: gives: nothing new to hold; the player now knows the company's price has no ceiling. Walt page: "Dan: if it's 'more than junk', call him first. 'They'd find a number.'"

40:3.8.1.text: That old tent of Walt's holding up?

40:3.8.c1.text: How do you know whose tent it is?

40:4.2.7.when: Thing: A canoe left on shore

40:4.3.2.text: Lot of country up here. Easy to get turned around.

40:4.3.3.text: Don't think so. Wade. I do security for the company. Parking lots, mostly. Fences.

40:4.3.c2.text: Were you out on {the lake of the search} yesterday?

40:4.3.4.text: Me? I don't go on the water. Never learned to like it.
40:4.3.4.if: True. He is never on the water. Walt page: "Wade says he doesn't go on the water."

40:4.3.7.text: I'd check. People get careless with their things up here.

40:4.3.8.text: That's me. Long time ago. I needed a place to park.
40:4.3.8.if: gives: confirmation; Walt page: "Wade is the W. Helstrom in the bunkhouse book. He said he needed a place to park."

40:4.3.9.if: gives: "Clean Boots is Wade." inks on the Walt page.

40:4.3.10.text: Somebody's got to keep this place in business.

40:4.3.11.text: Buys a dozen every week. I've never sold that man a hook.

40:4.4.1.text: Hey, so. Somebody phoned in a leech order for you. Which, I don't think it's for leeches?

item.leechslip.text:
PHONE ORDER
For: (the one with the old pack)
LEECH ORDER — 3 doz — Hog Creek
Ask for Maggie
Pd: —

40:4.4.2.text: No idea. She sounded nice? She said you'd know what it meant. She also asked if we had a good leech guy at Hog Creek, and we're not even Hog Creek.

40:4.4.3.text: This morning. Early. She said three dozen like it was important. Three. Not two, not four.

40:4.4.4.text: Just me. And now you. Do you want me to not tell people things? I can not tell people things.

40:5.c2.text: Two men, boots. Came by water.

40:6.2.1.text: There's a woman writes for that Duluth paper. The Ledger. She asked the right question once, in 2019. You mind if I call her?

40:6.2.2.text: I'll use the phone at the Legion. They've had the same phone since 1970. Nobody listens to it.

40:6.2.4.text: I called that woman from the Ledger. I've cut out her pieces for years. I hope that was all right. If it wasn't, it's done.

40:6.2.5.text: I called a reporter. Don't look at me like that. I've been reading page two to nobody for seven years.

40:6.2.6.text: I called that woman at the Duluth paper. Gene would've. He'd have done it from this phone, with the cord stretched out the door so nobody heard. So I did that.

40:6.2.7.text: Aili wouldn't. So I did. A reporter, the Duluth one. Don't tell her it was me. She'll know anyway.

40:6.2.8.text: The Ledger? Duluth. There's a woman writes about the leases for them. Tomczak. Comes through in the fall like a grouse hunter. Leave her a note at a counter, she'll find it.

paper.walt.2019.text:
Ask the state for Boreal's 1976 Kettle creek field sheets.
Ask why stations 7–12 are background.

paper.ostrander.1977.text:
Oct 3 '77 — 4:40 pm. Call. E. HAAPALA, Ely. Boreal crew, water sampler.
Says Q3 water report to state was changed. Stations 7–12 (below the pad)
moved to "background". Has the orig. field books + the mgr's pencil draft.
Also a cash book — D. Sorensen's?? Won't say more on this line.
Party line at the crew camp. Careful.
Where are they — "put away safe, up by Bald Eagle."
MEET Fri 14th, here, 2:00. Brother may come.

paper.ostrander.1977.blue.text:
[blue ink]
Fri 14 — no show.
Mon 17 — called crew camp. Missing since Wed. Canoe found swamped Fri a.m., Bald Eagle.
Mon 24 — found. Drowned, they say.
Nobody here wants it. — B.O.

paper.boreal.1976.text:
BOREAL RANGE MINERALS CO.
ANNUAL EXPLORATION REPORT — YEAR ENDING DEC. 31, 1976
SCHEDULE B: TARGETS
...
E-6   Kettle pad (west pads), SW of Bald Eagle L.   Bulk sample, trench; 14 holes    Active
E-7   Pietro L., hill above NE shore                  2 holes (packsack); 1 test pit   Dropped. No values.
                                                      Field report: E. Haapala
E-8   Gabbro L., S shore                              3 holes                          Dropped.
...

40:6.4.2.text: You'd be the one with the old pack. You didn't bring it. That's either smart or you forgot.

40:6.4.3.text: Most days. Sit, if you want. I'm told this is fishing.

40:6.4.c2.text: You've got a bobber on a bass plug.

40:6.4.5.text: I don't actually know what you do with leeches. I just needed a word nobody'd look at twice.

40:6.4.6.text: I write for the Ledger. Freelance, which means they pay me when they remember.

40:6.4.c4.text: What are you doing at Hog Creek?

40:6.4.7.text: Vacation. My cousin's got a place on the Kawishiwi. I'm up for the week.

40:6.4.c5.text: You said your cousin has a place. You're in the bunkhouse.

40:6.4.8.text: I don't have a cousin. I have a bunk and a rod I bought Tuesday.

40:6.4.9.text: I'm here because you've been asking the same questions I have. And because Hog Creek's quiet and nobody in Ely knows my car.
40:6.4.9.if: gives: trust; flag `maggieCaught`. She doesn't lie to the player again, about anything.

40:6.4.c6.text: How did you hear about me?

40:6.4.10.text: An older man called me. He didn't give his name. He didn't have to. He called it 'the outfit' four times in two minutes.

40:6.4.11.text: He said somebody's carrying Walt's pack and asking the right questions. I've been waiting seven years for somebody to ask the right questions.

40:6.4.12.text: Nothing from you. Not today. If you tell me where you've been, I have to write it down, and then I have to worry about it. Let's not.

40:6.4.13.text: I'll tell you what I've got. Then you know who to come to.

40:6.4.14.text: The company wants to mine on the old Boreal ground, south-west of Bald Eagle. Before they can, they have to show the state what the water was like before anybody touched it.

40:6.4.15.text: They're using Boreal's numbers from 1976. Those numbers say the creek below the old pad was dirty on its own. 'Naturally mineralised.' That gets you looser rules.

40:6.4.16.text: If the numbers are honest, fine. That's a fair fight and I'll write it straight.

40:6.4.17.text: If they aren't, somebody lied in 1976, and some of the same men are leaning on the lie now. The state decides this winter.

40:6.4.18.text: The story's about four or five men. Not the mine. Not the town. Men.

40:6.4.19.text: In 2019 somebody wrote me. No name. Ely postmark. I did what it said. The state sent me one list and 'not located' for the rest. I called the company for comment. They didn't comment.

40:6.4.21.text: That's his. Isn't it. The guide.

40:6.4.22.text: I called them for comment. That September. I always call for comment, it's the rule, you call.

40:6.4.23.text: He went in the lake in October.

40:6.4.24.text: Okay. New rule. I don't call anybody for comment until it's in my hand. And I don't ask you where you go. Not once.
40:6.4.24.if: gives: Walt page: "The letter to the Ledger in 2019 is in Walt's hand. Maggie called the company about it. Four weeks later he was gone." Flag `maggieMatched`. This is her confession; it is why she will wait, and why she offers to stop later.

40:6.4.25.text: Fine. Keep your cards. I'd keep mine.

40:6.4.26.text: Bill Ostrander had this beat before me. That's his. He waited for that kid all afternoon.

40:6.4.27.text: E-7. Pietro. Field report by Haapala. Somebody in that family dug a hole on Pietro in 1976. I don't know what it means. You might.

40:6.4.28.text: I'm not going to tell you it's safe. I don't know that it's safe.

40:6.4.29.text: If they're watching you, don't change anything. Fish. Buy bait. Be boring.

40:6.4.30.text: Not the paper. Not email. Leave a note at any counter. Leech order. The number of dozens is the number of days.

40:6.4.31.text: Three dozen, I come on the third morning, and every morning after till you show. I've got a thermos and nothing better to do.

40:6.4.32.text: My dad was at the plant thirty years. I'm not against mines. I'm against men who lie about water.

40:6.4.33.text: Don't tell me. Okay, tell me. I won't write it down.

40:6.4.34.text: Go on. You'll lose the light. I'll be here, failing at this.

40:6.5.2.text: You've got a look. Don't tell me where. Tell me if it's paper.
40:6.5.2.when: Last thing: A big finding since the last visit

40:6.5.3.text: You look like you slept in a canoe.
40:6.5.3.when: Last thing: The canoe adrift, if the player hasn't told her

40:6.5.4.text: There's a truck at the end of this road I don't like. Not for you. For me. I'm told it's a Ford.

40:6.5.5.text: Ice is out. So am I. How was your winter?

40:6.6.1.text: Day use. At a bunkhouse. He parked. Somebody should ask him what for, and it shouldn't be you.
40:6.6.1.when: The player has: The 2019 bunkhouse register, W. Helstrom, day use, parked

40:6.6.2.when: The player has: The 2019 bunkhouse register, W. Helstrom, day use, parked

40:6.6.3.text: Helstrom Site Services. Wade Helstrom. I've had his name on a sticky note for six years and never been able to put him anywhere. Now he's on the Isabella in August 2019.
40:6.6.3.when: The player has: The Isabella fuel receipt, Helstrom Site Services

40:6.6.4.text: Wade's firm was at the camp on the Isabella.
40:6.6.4.when: The player has: The Isabella fuel receipt, Helstrom Site Services

40:6.6.5.text: He signed his own name. At the funeral. Either he's stupid or he wanted somebody to see it. He isn't stupid.
40:6.6.5.when: The player has: Aili's guest book, W. Helstrom

40:6.6.7.text: Nobody printed this. Bill would have. He never knew it existed.
40:6.6.7.when: The player has: Ollie's 1977 search log

40:6.6.8.text: I could find out whose number that is in ten minutes. I'm not going to. You know these people. I don't. So it's his. I'm sorry.
40:6.6.8.when: The player has: The message pad page, with a Duluth number

40:6.6.9.when: The player has: Wade's number, from Denny after the reveal

40:6.6.10.text: If she'll say it with her name, it changes everything. She won't, and she's right not to. Don't ask her.

40:6.6.11.text: If he'll say it with his name, it runs with his name. Tell him I'll read it back to him first. Every word.
40:6.6.11.when: The player has: Tauno will go on record

40:6.6.12.text: That's legal's sentence. He's been handed it.

40:6.6.13.text: That's a picture of a creek. I need the paper that says why it's that colour.
40:6.6.13.when: The player has: A photo of the orange creek

40:6.6.14.text: Don't tell me where that is. I mean it. If I know, they can get it out of me.
40:6.6.14.when: The player has: Anything that places the far end, the shore, the landing sign, the camp

40:6.6.15.text: Bill used to say a story's a box of paper and a person who'll stand next to it. I've got half a box. You're the person, I think. I'm sorry about that.

40:6.6.17.text: If I know it, I have to decide what to do with it. I'd rather decide with the paper in front of me. Tell me then. Or don't.

40:6.7.2.text: We can stop. I mean that. No story's worth your canoe. I've got enough to write a column about old field sheets that nobody reads past the second paragraph.

40:6.7.3.text: Okay. Then we do it properly. When you have it, you don't stop anywhere, you don't sleep at a site, you don't call me. You come to one of two places at first light.

40:6.7.4.text: Think. I'll be here. Nothing's on a clock but them.

40:6.9.c1.text: If I found it, where would I bring it?

40:6.9.1.text: First thing. If you find it, don't bring it to me here. Not to any store. Stores have phones and people who talk on them.

40:6.9.2.text: Second. Bill's note says 'put away safe'. If it's a cache in the woods and you lift it, they'll know by dark. Don't ask me how. They always know by dark.

40:6.9.4.text: Lake One. It's a big lot, there's always somebody loading, and nobody looks at a grey wagon. It's a long way round from anywhere I'd guess, which is the point.

40:6.9.5.text: Or Little Gabbro, if you're in a hurry. It's faster. It's also the first place I'd watch, if I were them.

40:6.9.6.text: I don't do this. Don't tell anybody I did this.

40:6.9.7.text: When you know which, leave a leech order. Number of dozens is the days. I'll be in the lot at first light from that morning on, every morning, till you come out of the woods.

40:6.9.8.text: Lake One. But I'm not carrying it.

40:6.9.c3.text: What if I don't make it?

40:6.9.9.text: Then they'll have stopped you at a landing and been very polite about it. Go round another way. I'll still be in the lot.

40:6.9.c4.text: What happens when I give it to you?

40:6.9.10.text: I read it in the car with the doors locked. Then I drive to Duluth and don't stop. Two weeks, if it's what I think it is.

40:6.9.c5.text: What if the company finds out where?

40:6.9.11.text: They'll come. They'll stand in the lot and be nice. Let them. A lot full of witnesses at sunrise is the safest place in the state.

40:6.9.12.text: Nobody. Not your friends. Not the old men. Nobody. I mean that kindly. Especially not him.

40:6.9.13.text: Go on. Buy bait like a person who means to use it.

note.maggie.meet.text:
Too many trucks. Farm, tomorrow first light.
Leeches are on me.
— M.

40:6.9.14.text: There's a woman on the phone for you. She says she's forty minutes out and don't move.

40:7.2.1.text: New sign at the junction's been up ten years. Still the new sign.

40:7.2.2.text: State's going to decide on the company's plan this winter. They said that last winter.

40:7.2.3.text: My nephew drills for the company. Seasonal. Nine months a year he's a geologist and three he's my nephew.

40:7.2.4.text: We drove past a sign for a mining company. Is that, like, near here? Like near near?

40:7.2.5.text: Company's open house is the twenty-second. Half the town goes for the bars and the other half stands at the road with signs. Then they all have a bar.

40:7.2.6.text: When the drill crews were out, you'd see their canoes sit in a bay all day. Watching water. Waiting on a plane.

40:7.2.7.text: Fella was in asking which way you went. Said he was a friend of yours. I said you went fishing. That's what everybody does here.

40:7.2.8.text: Dan from the company was in. He's nice. He's, like, aggressively nice.

40:7.2.9.text: Len was asking after you. Len asks after everybody. It's his hobby.

40:7.2.10.text: There's two guys in a green canoe back on {lake}. No rods. They just sit there. Is that a thing people do?

40:7.2.11.text: Somebody's buying a lot of leeches and not catching anything. I'd like to know where he's dumping them.

40:7.2.12.text: There was a truck in the {EP} lot at six this morning. Engine running. Nobody in it went anywhere.

40:7.2.13.text: Len says you've been reading old state papers. Len says it like it's a hobby too.

40:7.2.14.text: Fella from the company asked me what lakes the old guides liked in the fall. I told him all of them.

40:7.2.15.text: Frank Kosir says he's retired. Retired men don't sleep days.

40:7.2.16.text: Company had a man at the Little Gabbro road end all week. Checking the gate, he said. There's no gate.

40:7.2.17.text: Your writer's still here. She's caught one perch in two weeks and she was proud of it.

40:7.2.18.text: That fella in the clean truck. He was at the Moose lot Tuesday and the Farm lot Wednesday. Busy man for somebody who doesn't fish.

40:7.2.19.text: That truck's been in our lot three mornings. Not one of mine. Not anybody's I know.

40:7.2.20.text: There's a guy at the end of the {portage}, sitting by a canoe, no gear. We said hi. He nodded. Just a nod.

40:7.2.21.text: Fall's quiet. That's the point of fall. Not so quiet this year.

40:7.2.22.text: Truck at the Crane landing again. Same one. You want to come in the back way, come in the back way.

40:7.2.23.text: Some guy called and asked when you'd be back. I said I'm not allowed to know things. That's true now. I made it true.

40:7.2.24.text: Somebody sitting in a canoe off the {portage} landing all day. In this cold. With no line in the water.

40:7.3.1.text: Party came off {lake}, said two fellas in a green Kevlar were asking after a solo.

40:7.3.2.text: This group from Madison came off {lake} all weird. Two guys asked them had they seen anybody alone. They thought it was romantic. It isn't, right?

40:7.3.3.text: Couple came off {lake}. Said there were two men on it with no rods, asking about a solo paddler. I said that's a lot of men for a lake that size.

40:7.3.4.text: You by yourself? Some guys on {lake} were asking about somebody by themselves. Was that you? It was kind of creepy, honestly.
40:7.3.4.when: Speaker: Weekend party, at a portage

40:7.3.5.text: Two fellas on {lake} asked my grandson had he seen a single canoe. Asked it twice. People who fish don't ask twice.

40:8.1.text: Nothing was ever drilled east of Bald Eagle.

40:8.2.text: Walt was never right after his brother.

40:8.4.text: My cousin's got a place on the Kawishiwi.

40:8.6.text: I don't go on the water
